column1: # `is` against a predicate type — the headline spelling for the membership
# a `fnpred` declaration creates, and the one shape of it that does not
# compile.
# A predicate type's constraint IS a function value, so asking `4 is Even`
# walks that value into `is` and hits the Stage 3 refusal "function value
# reaches is". The refusal is PRE-EXISTING and has nothing to do with
# `fnpred`: the capitalised-fn form this word replaces
# (`def Even fn n:Integer Boolean [...]`) refuses byte-identically, which is
# why no `is <predicate-type>` row exists anywhere in the main corpus today
# — the compiling shapes there reach membership through typed defs and
# typed params instead (lang/spec/fnpred.tsv, lang/spec/record.tsv §177).
# They live here rather than being dropped because `4 is Even` is what a
# reader will actually write, and the interpreter — the oracle — answers it
# correctly. Graduation: Stage 3 admitting a function value at `is`, at
# which point these rows move into lang/spec/fnpred.tsv beside the typed-def
# forms they mirror.
def Even fnpred n:Integer [eq 0 (mod 2 n)]  4 is Even
column3: an even Integer is a member

column1: def Even fnpred n:Integer [eq 0 (mod 2 n)]  5 is Even
def Even fnpred [[n:Integer] [eq 0 (mod 2 n)]]  4 is Even
column3: the spec-list form is the same type

column1: def Even fnpred [[n:Integer] [eq 0 (mod 2 n)]]  5 is Even
def Big fnpred n:Integer [n gt 10]  50 is Big
def Big fnpred n:Integer [n gt 10]  5 is Big
def Positive fnpred n:Integer [if (n gt 0) [n] [None]]  5 is Positive
column3: None-on-failure: a non-none result means member

column1: def Positive fnpred n:Integer [if (n gt 0) [n] [None]]  0 is Positive
